items.title: Jerry Blumberg Interview, 1961-04-06
items.q: Lawrence Marrero looked like a real rock of Gibraltar sitting there playing the banjo.

ctx.x: In the old style, New Orleans seating, they always had the drums on one end, so it wouldn't be right back at the trumpeter's head. He'd be separated with the trombonist in there between the drum and the coronet. Go ahead if you can go ahead with your lessons pretty soon. I mean, that's something else before that.

I'd like to talk a little about Bunk. I mean, my impression of Bunk as he looked. I mean, I remember the band, of course, was all sitting down. The whole band had a marvelous look about it. Lawrence Marrero looked like a real rock of Gibraltar sitting there playing the banjo. I remember he looked like the steadiest beat in town, you know. Even if you didn't hear him, you knew that the guy had to have a steady beat because he absolutely had this immobile smile, a Buddha-like smile. And he was a great-looking…
Had you ever heard that anyplace else before?
